reasons: Missing names return empty results silently.

terms.meaning: A tree of categories. Here it is the structure of an industry, from broad stages down to specific commodities.
One chooser option, a slice of an industry the user can pick.
A short lowercase identifier used in web addresses, such as nuclear.
The ordered stages of an industry, from the first step to the final product.
Any item below another item in a tree, including its children and their children.
A function that calls itself to work through a tree one level at a time.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and rules for segment options
sections.what: A comment block explaining what a segment is for two kinds of industry tree, and that the picker is turned on by a flag rather than by counting options. It also imports the industry lookup and settings helpers the rest of the file uses.
sections.why: The comment says counting cannot decide, because two industries with one option each can behave differently.
sections.watch_out: Adding more options to an industry does not show a picker; only the flag in its settings controls that.

sections.name: SegmentNode
sections.title: Shape of one segment option
sections.what: Describes one picker option as a name plus an optional group heading. The name is also the value saved in the web address as the segment parameter.
sections.why: The comments say the name is the value carried in the address.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a segment in the industry tree breaks any saved links that point to the old name.

sections.name: getSegmentNodes
sections.title: Build the picker list for an industry
sections.what: Returns the options to show in the segment picker for one industry. For value-chain industries each top-level stage is an option. For other industries, a top-level item whose children have children shows those children under its name as a group, and a plain top-level item is an option by itself.
sections.why: The comments explain the two tree shapes this function has to handle.
sections.watch_out: The group check only looks one level down, so a deeper tree may appear flatter than intended.

sections.name: collectNames
sections.title: Collect a node and all names under it
sections.what: Gathers the name of a tree node and the names of every node beneath it, moving down one level at a time. Its result is used to build the complete set of names for a chosen segment.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond serving the expansion function that calls it.
sections.watch_out: It assumes the tree has no loops; a loop in the data would make it repeat without end.

sections.name: findNode
sections.title: Find a node by name
sections.what: Searches the whole tree, top to bottom, for the first node with a given name, and returns that node or nothing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond locating a chosen segment.
sections.watch_out: If the same name appears twice in the tree, only the first match is used, with no warning.

sections.name: expandSegment
sections.title: Expand a chosen segment to all its names
sections.what: Takes an industry and a chosen segment name and returns that name plus every name below it. The result is the exact list used to match projects when filtering or counting. It returns an empty list when the segment is not in the tree.
sections.why: The comment says rows stored at the segment itself must also count, so the parent is included with its children.
sections.watch_out: An empty result is not an error, so a misspelled segment name can quietly return no projects. The code does not say how callers handle an empty list.

sections.name: hasSegmentChooser
sections.title: Check whether the picker is turned on
sections.what: Returns true only when the industry's settings explicitly turn on the segment picker. An industry with several options but no flag shows no picker.
sections.why: The comment explains the flag is separate because counting options cannot decide whether a picker appears.
sections.watch_out: A new industry that needs a picker must have the flag set in its settings, or the picker stays hidden.

summary: Builds the list of segment options for an industry's picker, and turns one chosen segment into the full set of names used to filter projects.
purpose: Lets a user pick a slice of an industry, such as one commodity, and see only the projects in that slice.
why: The header comments explain the two tree shapes and say the picker is turned on by an explicit flag, because counting options cannot decide.
how: Looks up the industry tree. For value-chain industries, each top-level stage is an option. For other industries, a top-level item whose children have children is a group, and its children become options under that group name; otherwise the top-level item is an option by itself. To filter, it finds the chosen node anywhere in the tree and collects its name and every name beneath it. A separate check reads the picker flag.
inputs: An industry slug (a short text id such as nuclear or mining-metals) and, for filtering, a segment name.
outputs: A list of options, each with a name and an optional group, or a list of names for filtering, or a yes or no for whether the picker shows.
risks: Segment names must match exactly. A name that is not found gives an empty list with no message. The group rule only looks one level down. A duplicate name in the tree resolves to the first match. A loop in the tree data would never finish.
debug: If a picker is missing, check the industry's picker flag. If filtering shows nothing, check the segment name spelling against the industry tree and check the slug. Tree problems appear in the industry structure file, which this file imports.
